text:
lisa: Heads up — after rolling NVIDIA driver 535.101 -> 550.22 in the us-west-2 dedicated GPU pool last night, we're seeing a spike of TensorRT build failures and xFormers/FlashAttention illegal memory access on H100 nodes.

omar: saw the alerts. NCCL timeouts in some all-reduce jobs too. H100s in pool-2 seem most affected, A100s less so.

devon: can you paste a sample failure?

lisa: here's a crash log from a failed TRT perf build (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17 03:12:45] TRT: ERROR: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: illegal memory access
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  TRT::Engine::build failed
```

anita: same stacktrace from our nightly evals in us-west-2b. Also seeing xformers kernels throwing `runtime_error: cuBLAS status 13` when fused attention path is selected.

maya: rolling forward driver across thousands of GPUs is the risk we talked about. Was there a kernel module change that could affect cuBLAS/FlashAttention ABI?

omar: driver release notes mention CUDA 12.2 runtime + some kernel ABI tweaks for SM8.x, but nothing explicit. My guess: new driver interacts poorly with certain cuBLAS/cuDNN binary combos used by our TRT/xformers builds.

deploy-bot: job 9824 - rollback request queued for pool-2 (priority: high)

lisa: I'm pausing the rest of the rollouts. Can infra/dev-runtime confirm whether a quick driver rollback to 535.101 resolves the failures? We need to avoid large evictions for customer-facing nodes.

devon: spun up a small canary cluster (3 H100s) and repro'd. Rolling back to 535.101 fixed the TRT build and xformers attention errors on the canary. Confirmed NCCL hangs also disappear.

anita: good repro. Do we have a mitigation that doesn't require full rollback? Maybe force non-fused attention path or pin specific cuBLAS/Trt binaries?

omar: possible but risky at scale — many customers rely on TensorRT optimized graphs for latency. Forcing unfused kernels increases CPU/GPU time and costs. We should weigh cost delta.

maya: cost note — if we fallback to non-fused, estimated 15-25% tokens/sec drop on H100 TF workloads -> extra capacity required temporarily (~+10% GPUs), TCO impact ~$12k/week for current fleet.

lisa: action plan proposal: 1) pause rollout (done), 2) rollback pool-2 to 535.101 during low-traffic window, 3) create reproducible regression test in CI for driver/kernel combos, 4) coordinate with NVIDIA for root cause, 5) prepare fallback build (non-fused) for emergency toggle. Thoughts?

omar: +1. Also add automated canary warmup and kernel smoke tests (xformers/FlashAttention/TensorRT) to deploy pipeline before any future driver rollouts.

devon: I'll open an infra-ops PR to add the smoke tests and a script that runs TRT build + sample attention ops on a small canary matrix (A100/H100 + drivers 535/550).

anita: I'll draft the rollback runbook. Include telemetry queries to find affected tenants and mark any high-priority jobs to preemptively reschedule.

lisa: pinging @sre-bot to create an incident and notify oncall.

sre-bot: Incident I-2026-0317 created: "Driver 550 rollout -> TensorRT/xFormers kernel failures (us-west-2)". Notifying oncall and owners.

lisa: thanks. Let's stay in this thread for updates. If anyone finds a minimal repro harness that pinpoints whether it's cuBLAS vs driver kernel ABI, drop it here.

omar: FYI — I opened NV ticket 12345678 with logs + repro steps. NV engineer asked for `nvidia-bug-report` archives and exact libcudnn/cuBLAS versions.

maya: scheduling rollback during 02:00-03:30 UTC tomorrow. I'll coordinate with oncall and CS for customer communication.

devon: PR for smoke tests incoming. I'll also add an automated rollback gate if canary fails 3x in a row.

lisa: perfect. After rollback and smoke-tests, we should re-run driver upgrade in a staggered, region-by-region strategy with expanded metric KPIs (kernel errors, TRT build failures, NCCL latencies).

anita: recording: affected pools -> us-west-2 pool-2 (H100-heavy), us-west-2b dev-nightly. No reports from eu-central or apac yet.

maya: note to sales/support: we may need to proactively notify a few enterprise customers running dedicated H100 clusters. I'll draft language once rollback confirmed.

lisa: thanks all. Keep logs and canary artifacts in the incident ticket.
